info.description:
Australian racing odds, prices, and results.

All endpoints are relative to this document's server URL and require an API key
in the `X-API-Key` header. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents carrying a
stable `code` you can branch on. Collections are cursor-paginated:
follow `next` rather than constructing page parameters.

The intended workflow is bootstrap, then follow: take a snapshot of the scope you
care about with `GET /snapshot` (or one race with
`GET /events/{id}/snapshot`), then connect `GET /stream`
with `snapshot=none` and the `cursor` it returned. Each odds
row names `key` (`win` or `place`) so you can
render a race card without joining a market collection. Stream frames are
unmetered, so following is cheaper and faster than polling.

Empty collections are always `[]`, never `null`.

This contract only grows. New fields and new endpoints can appear at any time,
so ignore fields you do not recognise; existing fields will not be removed,
retyped, or moved, and a breaking change would ship as a new path prefix.

get.description:
A resumable stream of everything changing in the races you filter for.

Start by bootstrapping over REST — `GET /snapshot` for a scope, or `GET /events/{id}/snapshot` for one race — then connect with `snapshot=none` and the `cursor` that response returned. That is the fast, resumable path and the one to build on.

`snapshot=full` streams the current state as frames before going live, so one connection needs no REST call. It requires an `event`, `meeting`, or `venue` filter: on a broader scope it takes minutes, has no resumable position until `sync`, and starts over on any drop, so it is refused rather than offered as a trap.

Every frame's SSE id is a cursor. Reconnect with it in `Last-Event-ID` (or the `cursor` parameter) to resume exactly where you stopped. `ping` frames arrive throughout, including while a bootstrap is still building. On a `resync` frame, bootstrap again over REST and reconnect with the `cursor` that response returned. Frames are not metered.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the REST bootstrap or prior SSE frame.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Fresh-connection bootstrap: 'full' (default) streams current state then a sync frame, and requires an event, meeting, or venue filter; 'none' emits only a ready frame for clients that bootstrapped over REST.
parameters.name: snapshot

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the last received SSE frame; takes precedence over cursor.
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

parameters.description: Repeatable market key filter: win or place.
parameters.name: market

schema.description: Every frame carries an opaque cursor in its SSE id.
